newsitem.title: CANADA: Sears Canada hits new highs in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Sears Canada hits new highs in heavy trade.

text.p: Shares in Sears Canada Inc soared to all-time highs on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday as investors snapped up stock in the rebounding Canadian department store retailer.
Sears Canada topped the TSE's most-active list at midday, climbing 0.55 to 11.75 in turnover of 1.8 million shares. The retailer's stock earlier hit a 52-week high of 12.

"Investors are clearly confident that things have turned and that they (Sears) are going to make some money in the next couple of years," said Bill Chisholm, an analyst with Deacon Capital Corp in Toronto.
Chisholm said the sluggish Canadian economy appears to be getting stronger, while Sears has drastically cut costs over the last year.

Toronto-based Sears Canada posted sharply lower third quarter losses last month as a result of downsizing, store remodelling and layoffs. Sears reported a C$555,000 loss in the three months ended September 28, compared to a loss of C$2.9 million in the same period a year earlier.
Investors have also cheered the recent hiring of chief executive officer Paul Walters, a former chief executive of Zellers Inc, a unit of Sears rival Hudson's Bay Co.
"He (Walters) ran Zellers for quite a while and knows the challenges of running a department store in Canada," Chisholm said.
Canadian retailers have faced tough competition since U.S. giant Wal-Mart Stores Inc invaded Canada in 1994.
